title: renewal-failure-mode-analysis-and-ops-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook is an operational guide for diagnosing why a renewal is at risk (failure-mode analysis), triaging root causes, and selecting the minimal effective save or mitigation that preserves revenue and long-term adoption. It is intentionally pragmatic — includes templates, quick decision heuristics, and an incident-style escalation ladder for exec engagement.

Scope and audience:
- Owner: CSM and AM teams; tactical ops for Customer Success Managers and Renewal Specialists.
- When to use: at the first signal of renewal deterioration (30–90 days before renewal) and during QBR prep for at-risk accounts.
- Not in scope: contractual/legal negotiations that require Legal/Economic adjustments (escalate those to Legal).

Quick overview (TL;DR):
1) Run failure-mode checklist to identify primary driver(s) (adoption, ROI, product incidents, pricing, org changes).
2) Score risk (0–100) and map to one of three intervention tiers: Prevent, Mitigate, Rescue.
3) Run the recommended play(s) in the 48–72hr decision window and record outcome in the Renewal Tracker.
4) If score >= 75 or rapid deterioration, trigger Exec Escalation ladder.

Failure-mode checklist (one-pass diagnostic):
- Product usage: weekly active users, key feature usage down >30% in 60 days? (Y/N)
- Value delivery: customer-reported blockers in roadmap items or metrics not improving (NPS/CSAT decline)?
- Recent incidents: Sev1/Sev2 in last 90 days? (Y/N)
- Spend anomalies: sudden drop in calls/requests to API or migration away to other providers?
- Contract/Org signals: procurement hold, re-org, hiring freeze?
- Relationship health: no QBR scheduled, low executive engagement, renewal rep not assigned?

Scoring rubric (simple, repeatable):
- Usage (0–30): 30 = full drop-off; 0 = healthy adoption
- Value (0–30): 30 = clear unmet ROI; 0 = ROI confirmed
- Reliability/Incidents (0–20): 20 = repeated or unresolved Sev1/2; 0 = none
- Commercial/Org (0–20): 20 = procurement hold or exec churn; 0 = contract stable
Total score = sum (0–100).
Risk bands and immediate actions:
- Low (0–34): monitor + preventative play (owner: CSM)
- Medium (35–74): targeted mitigation + AM/SE involvement within 7 days
- High (75–100): full rescue + exec escalation (within 48–72 hours)

Intervention categories and sample plays:
A) Preventative plays (Low band) — quick, lightweight, focussed on re-engagement
- Habit-building nudges: 30-min product clinic, in-app walkthrough refresh, checklist for power users. Owner: CSM (2–7 day cadence).
- Goal reset: align on 90-day success metrics and simple milestones (one-pager). Owner: CSM & Solutions Engineer.
- Micro-training series: tailored short videos + office hours.

B) Mitigation plays (Medium band) — medium-effort; aim to restore confidence
- Value workshop: 60–90 minute ROI workshop with customer stakeholders + technical health check. Deliverable: ROI memo + 30/60/90 plan. Owner: AM + SE.
- Ops remediation: address integration issues, spike in error rates, or quota/limits. Temporary quota increases or dedicated debug sprint. Owner: SRE/Support + SE.
- Pilot expansion: add a small paid pilot for a missing feature area to rebuild momentum. Owner: Product + AM (requires quick SOW).

C) Rescue plays (High band) — high-touch, time sensitive
- White-glove remediation: 5-day war room with daily standups, dev + SE + CSM, progress notes to customer.
- Executive sponsorship: bilateral call between customer exec sponsor and our VP/Director. Provide a short executive remediation brief.
- Contract accommodation: short-term credit, limited pricing adjustment, or milestone-based extension (Legal approval required).

Escalation ladder (timing & triggers):
- Level 1 (CSM): initial diagnosis and mitigation execution. Trigger: Risk >= 35.
- Level 2 (AM/Head of Accounts + SE): coordinate mitigations, run ROI workshop. Trigger: Risk >= 50 or no improvement in 7 days.
- Level 3 (Director VP CS + Product Lead): propose product remediation roadmaps and prioritize fixes. Trigger: Risk >= 70 or unresolved Sev1.
- Level 4 (Exec): CRO/CEO involvement for contract-level decisions (credits/renegotiation). Trigger: Risk >= 85 or strategic account at stake.

- Escalation process: short write-up + 1-page exec brief (see template below) -> Slack ping to #cs-escalations -> 30-min triage -> assign owners and due dates -> update tracker.

Exec brief template (one page, 15-minute read):
- Account snapshot: ARR, ACV, last 12mo trend lines
- Primary failure modes (top 3) and evidence
- Short-term ask (what we need now) and long-term ask (what we need from product/legal)
- Proposed save package and estimated cost to company
- Decision requested (approve/decline/modify) + deadline

Sample templated outreach: 48–72hr rescue email to customer exec:
Subject: Immediate plan to stabilize [AccountName] ahead of renewal
Body: Hi [ExecName], we’ve identified three operational gaps affecting [customer outcome]. We propose a focused 5-day remediation starting [date]. Deliverables: daily progress notes, ROI memo, and a proposal for a short-term accommodation to protect your deployment. Can you confirm a 30-minute alignment call this week?

Renewal tracker (pasteable CSV header + example row) — store canonical copy in the Renewal sheet linked above:
headers: account_name, account_owner, acv, renewal_date, risk_score, risk_band, primary_failure_modes, last_qbr_date, next_steps, current_play, play_owner, escalation_level, notes
example: "Acme Corp", "J. Lee", "$180k", "2025-06-30", "78", "High", "adoption;org-change", "2024-11-12", "5-day war room", "Asha Patel", "Level 3", "VP sponsor assigned; daily standups started"

Meeting runbook for a 45-min Renewal Rescue QBR:
- 0–5min: quick context + objectives (CSM)
- 5–20min: health metrics + top failure modes (data-driven; SE)
- 20–35min: remediation plan options + owner commitments (AM/Product)
- 35–40min: decision + next steps (1–3 granular actions)
- 40–45min: confirm exec sponsor and communication cadence

Decision matrix (one-line heuristics):
- If usage drop + unresolved incidents -> Rescue (war room + SE)
- If low exec engagement + procurement hold -> Exec escalation + legal consult
- If ROI unclear but stable usage -> Mitigate (ROI workshop)

Operational artifacts to attach to each at-risk record:
- Raw telemetry (last 90 days), detailed incident timeline, QBR slide deck, ROI memo draft, recorded calls (if available), and the owner’s 48hr action log.

Post-save review (5–10 days after action completion):
- Was renewal retained? (Y/N)
- What play(s) ran and owner(s)?
- Time to measurable improvement (days)
- Cost to company (credits, engineering time, exec time)
- Lessons learned and recommended permanent fixes

Metrics & dashboards to monitor (CS console):
- Renewal risk distribution by cohort (30/60/90 day buckets)
- % of high-risk accounts with active remediation plan within 72 hours
- Time-to-first-action after signal (target <48 hours)
- Win rate post-rescue (target >70% for High band)

Open questions / known gaps (notes to product and ops):
- Need a short SRE SLA for temporary quota increases and clear pricing for ad-hoc capacity boosts. (Ticket JIRA-CS-4821)
- Template for quick SOWs for pilot expansions — legal turnaround target 3 business days.
- Better telemetry slice for executive-level ROI snapshots (Product).

Next steps (ownerable):
- CSMs: start using the failure-mode checklist for next 10 flagged accounts (owner: Asha). Due: 2025-02-02.
- AMs + SEs: pilot the 5-day war room for two High-risk accounts; capture time/cost. Due: 2025-02-09.
- Ops: add 'time-to-first-action' to the CS dashboard and configure alert at 48 hours. Due: 2025-02-16.

Notes & informal / working items: 
- This doc is intentionally compact. Keep it lightweight and copy into account folders when starting a save.
- Use the linked Renewal sheet for canonical tracking; DO NOT keep local spreadsheets.
- Feedback loop: annotate this doc with examples from each rescue (collaborators listed above).

Change log (high-level):
